exp(i*t*k^3) defines S on periodic distributions for every real t and agrees with exp(-t*partial_x^3); no solution property is assumed.
The zero Fourier coefficient defines a constant distribution; the spatial mean has a legitimate domain.
P=I-P0 unambiguously depends on D005.
The inverse multiplier has an explicit zero-mode value; D^(-2) is its square. Invertibility on constants is not asserted.
The quadratic formula matches scheme (2). For L2 input, Dinv f lies in H1, so its squared factors are legitimate; estimates remain proved results.

All four cubic terms, coefficients, signs, propagator arguments and endpoint order match scheme (2). tau>0 guards division; f^2 is L1 for its mean, and all other products involve inverse derivatives in H1.
The unfiltered recurrence and initialization match the problem. Positive integer L and explicit H001 imply tau=T/L>0 in the theorem context. No stability or convergence is granted by definition.
Continuous integrands and tau>0 make the averages well defined for real phases. Covariance bounds are not assumed.

The polynomial Fourier formula is finite, with explicit k!=0 and a+b!=0 guards, phases and zero output. Extension is deferred to N004; zero-input vanishing follows directly from the covariance definition.
B is initially defined on smooth inputs, where products and differentiation are legitimate; no L2 bound is granted.
J has explicit inverses, propagators and mean projection. L2 inputs give legitimate inverse-derivative products; the normal-form identity remains N005.
The time integral includes both projections and the inverse derivative in its third slot. Smooth paths give its initial domain; estimates and rough extension remain N006.
p_star=23/14 and both norm components are specified. Restriction to paths with finite displayed norms defines a domain, and does not grant regularity to arbitrary paths.
The piecewise exponent includes 1/8 at gamma=1/2 and explicitly requires H002. Product and stage estimates remain N006.
The integral initially uses smooth time-independent mean-zero input, tau>0, and a stated step interval. The L2 extension is a proved property rather than a new root.

The smooth step tuple, W_n correction, Y_n, residual increment and residual initial value are explicit. tau>0 guards division. Endpoint agreement and continuity of concatenation are expressly left to N007.

The retained bundle faithfully restates the six same-source flow results, distinguishing the source equation, normalized homogeneous norms and positive/zero exponent cases. The sign/reflection and inhomogeneous-norm bridge is assigned to N001.
